successors.note: Infobox 'Succeeded by: Ottoman Empire'. From 1390 the island was a Venetian colony, so the republic-of-venice dossier loses it in 1470.

capitals.name: Chalkis (Negroponte, Chalkida)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Chalkis'; Chalkis was the shared capital, not under any single triarch. Jacques of Avesnes fortified it.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the infobox gives 'Principality established: 1204'; Cliopatria's shape begins in 1206. The island is the whole territory the page names (Boniface granted it as a fief to Jacques II of Avesnes, who fortified Chalkis), so the keyframe is the whole of Euboea.

Use the whole island.

correction.text: all of Euboea: the three triarchies of Oreos, Chalkis and Karystos, held by Ravano dalle Carceri, Giberto dalle Carceri and Pecoraro da Mercanuovo from mid-1205

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1210-1316, a period Cliopatria's row lacks: the row stops in 1209 and from 1210 its Euboean cells (8) sit inside the Republic of Venice row. The page has the island a Venetian protectorate from March 1209 ('protectorate of Venice, 1209-1390') and, from May 1209, a vassal of the Latin emperor; it stays one island throughout. The war of 1256-58 (William of Achaea took Chalkis; Venice retook it in early 1258) and Licario's Byzantine occupation to 1296 are contest events, not changes of the shape.

correction.text: the whole island under the triarchs and the Venetian protectorate

correction.text: the island without Karystos, held by the Catalan Company

correction.text: the whole island, Karystos again with the rest, under Venice as protector and from 1390 as colony

region.text: the island of Euboea, capital Chalkis

ledger.note: 1204: Euboea becomes a crusader fief after the partition of the Byzantine Empire. Infobox 'Principality established: 1204'; the state was established on Euboea 'after the partition of the Byzantine Empire following the Fourth Crusade'. Boniface of Montferrat, King of Thessalonica, received Euboea and granted it as a fief to Jacques II of Avesnes, who fortified Chalkis (the grant is undated; Cliopatria's row begins in 1206).

region.text: the island, now in three triarchies

ledger.note: Mid-1205: Jacques of Avesnes dies and Euboea passes to three Veronese barons: Ravano dalle Carceri, Giberto dalle Carceri and Pecoraro da Mercanuovo, who split it into Oreos (north), Karystos (south) and Chalkis (central); Chalkis was the shared capital. By 1209 Ravano was sole ruler, styling himself 'dominus insulae Nigropontis'.

region.text: Chalkis and the northern and central triarchies

ledger.note: June 1256: two triarchs break with Achaea. On 14 June 1256 Guglielmo of Verona and Narzotto dalle Carceri renounced allegiance to William II of Villehardouin and pledged themselves to Venice (War of the Euboeote Succession, begun by the death of Carintana dalle Carceri in 1255). The page does not date William's capture of Chalkis, which came before early 1258, so the declaration stands in for the first campaign (a bridging date); mirrors principality-of-achaea /ledger 11.

region.text: Chalkis and the northern and central triarchies

ledger.note: Early 1258: Venice retakes Chalkis, which William had captured; the Achaean victory at Karydi (May/June 1258) ends the war on the mainland, Doge Reniero Zeno negotiates peace in 1259 and a 1262 treaty recognises William's suzerainty. No land changed hands; mirrors principality-of-achaea /ledger 14.

region.text: most of the island, taken by the Byzantine admiral Licario

ledger.note: 1278: Licario's Byzantine occupation of most of Euboea. The Triarchy page's table lists the Nicaean (Byzantine) occupation as '1278–1285/96' with Licario as vice-governor; the prose says only that Licario left 'sometime after 1280' and that 'By 1296, Boniface of Verona had completely expelled the Byzantines from Euboea'. The extent ('most of') is my reading. [Reviewer eu-05-d, 2026-10-19: year 1276 to 1278 and confidence 1 to 2 from the page's table; 1276 was the principality-of-achaea dossier's.]

By 1296: Boniface of Verona has expelled the Byzantines from Euboea (Triarchy page: by 1296 Boniface of Verona had expelled the Byzantines from Euboea; Licario left after 1280). The year is the page's 'by'; the byzantine-empire dossier carries no Euboean events yet.

region.text: Karystos and the southern end of the island, the southern triarchy

ledger.note: 1317: Karystos falls to the Catalan Company. Karystos fell to the Catalan Company in 1317 and a 1319 treaty let Don Alfonso keep it (Triarchy page); the southern end of the island is the 35 km disc round Karystos, my reading of the southern triarchy.

region.text: Karystos and the southern end of the island, the southern triarchy

ledger.note: 1365: Venice acquires Karystos, reuniting the island. Venice acquired Karystos in 1365 (Triarchy page); the page names Venice, not the triarchy, as the buyer and does not name the seller (Don Alfonso's line, by the 1319 treaty), so the gain is drawn as the island's reunion under its Venetian protector.

1390: the last triarch's lands pass to Venice and Negroponte becomes a Venetian colony. the last triarchs died in 1383 and 1390 and left their lands to Venice; infobox 'protectorate of Venice, 1209-1390; then a Venetian colony, 1390-1470'. The page does not say which triarchy went in 1383.
12 July 1470: Mehmed II takes Chalkis. Mehmed II took Chalkis and the whole island came under Ottoman control (Triarchy page).
12 July 1470: Negroponte ends with the Ottoman conquest of Chalkis (infobox end 1470; 'succeeded by the Ottoman Empire').

wars.name: Lombard rebellion against Henry of Flanders
wars.outcome: Ravano dalle Carceri allied with the failed Lombard revolt, then in March 1209 recognised Venetian overlordship and in May 1209 acknowledged vassalage to the Latin Empire; Henry ended the feudal dependency of Negroponte on Thessalonica in 1208-09.
wars.note: The Triarchy page does not date the revolt; the Kingdom of Thessalonica page (opened for that dossier) puts Henry's campaign and the end of the vassals' dependency in 1208-09. No land changed hands.

wars.name: War of the Euboeote Succession

zones.text: Chalkis and the northern and central triarchies

wars.outcome: William II of Villehardouin captured Chalkis, Venice retook it in early 1258, William won at Karydi in May/June 1258, Doge Reniero Zeno negotiated peace in 1259 and a 1262 treaty recognised William's suzerainty over the triarchs.
wars.note: Begun by the death of Carintana dalle Carceri in 1255; on 14 June 1256 Guglielmo of Verona and Narzotto dalle Carceri renounced allegiance to William and pledged themselves to Venice.

wars.name: Byzantine campaigns on Euboea under Licario
wars.outcome: Licario left after 1280 and by 1296 Boniface of Verona had expelled the Byzantines from Euboea.
wars.note: The page's table dates the Byzantine occupation '1278–1285/96' (Licario vice-governor); the prose gives 'after 1280' for Licario's departure and 'By 1296' for the expulsion. [Reviewer eu-05-d, 2026-10-19: from 1276 to 1278.]

wars.name: Catalan Company's conquest of Karystos

zones.text: Karystos and the southern end of the island, the southern triarchy

wars.outcome: Karystos fell to the Catalan Company in 1317 and a 1319 treaty let Don Alfonso keep it; Venice bought it in 1365.

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of Negroponte
wars.outcome: On 12 July 1470 Mehmed II took Chalkis and the whole island came under Ottoman control.

certainty.note: An island: its coast is its border. Soft inside: the three triarchies (later six sestieri after 1216) are not drawn, and the Byzantine-held parts of 1276-96 and the Catalan end of 1317-65 are only as exact as the page's town names.

notes: Pages opened for this state: two (budget 1-2), plus the Kingdom of Thessalonica page opened for its own dossier. Cliopatria's Wikipedia field 'Negroponte' is a disambiguation page; identity.wikipedia is the article 'Triarchy of Negroponte'. Cliopatria row: 'Negroponte' 1206-1209 (9-10 cells, 2,178 km2) starts two years after the 1204 founding, ends 261 years before the Ottoman conquest of 1470 and omits the Karystos end of the island; from 1210 the Republic of Venice row contains the same Euboean cells (8 of them), so the island is drawn as Venice's own land for 1210-1470 unless the venice dossier removes it. This dossier therefore carries the island through 1470 (keyframes 1210, 1317, 1365). Not settled: (1) the vassal chain is carried by the suzerains: kingdom-of-thessalonica (1205-1209), latin-empire (vassal_start May 1209) and Venice (March 1209, protectorate to 1390, colony 1390-1470: needs vassal_start/vassal_end negroponte in the republic-of-venice dossier, eu-13), principality-of-achaea (1262-1278); (2) the byzantine-empire dossier has no Euboean events for Licario's occupation (start 1276 unverified, end by 1296); (3) the catalan-company dossier needs Karystos from 1317 (to 1365, not 1362); (4) the ottoman-empire dossier (me-10) needs Euboea in 1470; (5) the 1216 settlement into six sestieri (Ravano's death, the Venetian bailo) is not drawn; (6) which triarchy passed to Venice in 1383 is not on the page; (7) the size mismatch: the gazetteer's Euboea region is about 4,550 km2 against the infobox's 3,660 km2 and its southern edge (38.12N) stops short of Karystos (38.01N). Gazetteer names needed: Karystos (place, 38.01N 24.42E, Euboea) is a radius here. Family 'italy' (Veronese barons, then Venice) is a key of colours.json.
